primitives.meaning: a named business process that cannot safely proceed, and the specific field, document or value it is waiting on
entryFilters: a named business process that cannot safely proceed, and the specific field, document or value it is waiting on
no instance of this journey is already open for the the business entity that is blocked plus the specific missing requirement
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

primitives.does: Identify the exact missing item and the named process it blocks. A request that cannot name what it unblocks is progressive profiling wearing a blocker's clothes, and the two must not be confusable

primitives.asks: Can an authoritative source supply this without asking anyone?

branches.label: We already have it
branches.test: an authoritative system holds it, or it can be derived or reconciled from what we hold

branches.label: It has to be provided
branches.test: no system holds it and someone has to supply it

primitives.does: Retrieve and reconcile it. Asking someone for what we already hold authoritatively is the fastest way to demonstrate that we do not know our own records

primitives.asks: Who can actually supply the missing item?

branches.label: The customer or account holder
branches.test: only the person the record is about holds it, or policy requires it from them directly

branches.label: Someone inside the organisation
branches.test: an internal owner, team or operator holds it, or is the one authorised to produce it

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Request it from the person the record is about, stating what it unblocks, so the request is answerable rather than merely received
primitives.brief: Request it from the person the record is about, stating what it unblocks, so the request is answerable rather than merely received
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.does: Raise the request as owned work against the internal party who holds the item, carrying the blocked process and the running deadline. Routing an internal dependency down a customer channel asks the wrong person on a route they never agreed to

primitives.reads: the the business entity that is blocked plus the specific missing requirement re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

primitives.asks: Is what we now have valid?

branches.label: Invalid or incomplete
branches.test: what arrived does not satisfy the requirement

primitives.does: Persist it and re-evaluate the blocked process, which resumes because its dependency is satisfied rather than because it was told to

primitives.state: requirement satisfied; the blocked process is free to continue
primitives.reEntry: a further missing requirement is its own dependency with its own instance

primitives.asks: Given how critical the blocked process is, what now?

branches.label: Critical enough for a person
branches.test: the process matters enough that someone should own getting this resolved

branches.label: An alternate route exists
branches.test: the process can proceed by a path that does not require this item

branches.label: Not worth pursuing further
branches.test: the blocked process can wait or be abandoned without harm

primitives.on: a critical dependency that requesting did not resolve
carries: the missing item, who was asked, and what is blocked
what has already been tried, so the person does not repeat the request that failed

primitives.state: blocked process proceeding by a route that does not need this
primitives.reEntry: if the alternate route later requires it after all, that is a new dependency

primitives.state: requirement unmet; the blocked process stays blocked and says so
primitives.reEntry: the item arriving later re-opens this normally; it is not re-requested repeatedly in the meantime
